title: 诚实的重要 · 分级读物 (HSK 3)
source_material: The Importance of Being Earnest, Oscar Wilde (1895), retold as narrative prose. Researched from the play's full event chain (all three acts) rather than a remembered outline.

localization.the pun: Wilde's engine is Ernest (name) = earnest (honest). Chinese uses 诚 (Chéng): a real given name that also means honest/sincere. So 'I could only love a man named 诚' works, and the final reveal — he IS 诚 — still lands.

swaps.cigarette case: an engraved 手表 (watch) — the inscription from 西西 exposes the double life; 烟盒 is above level and cigarettes are wrong for a learner book
swaps.Bunbury: 班先生, an invented sick friend far away whom 阿龙 must 'visit'
swaps.christening: 改名字 — going to 陈先生 to change one's name, which carries the comedy better in Chinese than baptism
swaps.cucumber sandwiches / muffins: 蛋糕 — the same running joke of eating everything while discussing serious matters
swaps.three-volume novel: 一本很长的小说 left in the baby carriage

bible.logline: Two young men each invent a second identity to escape their duties; both end up courting women who will only marry a man named 诚 — and the lie turns out to be the truth.

cast.杰克: Jack. Serious guardian in the country, carefree '诚' in the city. Was found as a baby in a bag. Speaks earnestly, worries a lot.
cast.阿龙: Algernon. Jack's friend, clever and lazy, always eating. Invents 班先生 to escape dull dinners. Speaks lightly, teases.
cast.高文: Gwendolen. Loves 杰克; fixed on the name 诚. Certain of herself, a little grand.
cast.西西: Cecily. Jack's young ward. Bored by lessons, romantic, keeps a diary. Bright and stubborn.
cast.高太太: Lady Bracknell. Gwendolen's mother. Interrogates, disapproves, decides everything by money and family.
cast.白老师: Miss Prism. Cecily's teacher, strict, hiding an old mistake. Fond of 陈先生.
cast.陈先生: Dr Chasuble. Kind village gentleman, helps people change their names, fond of 白老师.
cast.班先生: Mr Ban. Algernon's imaginary sick friend — never appears.

relationships: 杰克 is 西西's guardian; 白老师 is her teacher
阿龙 is 高文's cousin; 高太太 is 高文's mother
杰克 loves 高文; 阿龙 loves 西西
白老师 and 陈先生 quietly like each other
unknown to all: 杰克 is 高太太's sister's son, so 阿龙's elder brother
setting: the country house and its garden
陈先生's small office in the village
events: 1. In the city flat 阿龙 eats all the cake while waiting for guests; 杰克 arrives and says he will ask 高文 to marry him
2. 阿龙 produces a watch 杰克 left behind, engraved 'to uncle 杰克, from 西西' — and demands to know who 杰克 and 西西 are
3. 杰克 confesses: in the country he is 杰克, guardian of 西西; he invented a bad younger brother 诚 in the city so he can escape
4. 阿龙 admits the same trick — his sick friend 班先生, whom he must 'visit' whenever a dinner is dull
5. 高文 and 高太太 arrive; alone with 高文, 杰克 proposes and she accepts
6. 高文 explains she could only love a man named 诚 — the name itself sounds honest
7. 高太太 interrogates 杰克: money, house, parents; he admits he was found as a baby in a bag at the station
8. 高太太 refuses; 高文 secretly asks for his country address; 阿龙 quietly writes it down too
9. In the country, 西西 avoids her lessons with 白老师 and daydreams about the wicked brother 诚
10. 白老师 and 陈先生 talk in the garden, awkward and fond
11. 阿龙 arrives at the country house calling himself 诚; 西西 is delighted to meet him
12. 杰克 comes home in black to announce that his brother 诚 has died — and finds 阿龙 alive as 诚
13. 杰克 orders 阿龙 to leave; 阿龙 refuses because he likes 西西
14. 阿龙 proposes to 西西; she says they have been engaged for months
15. 西西 shows her diary: letters she wrote to herself, an engagement she broke off once and mended, all before they met
16. 西西 adds she could only marry a man named 诚
17. Separately, both men arrange with 陈先生 to change their names to 诚 that same week
18. 高文 arrives; she and 西西 take tea, coldly polite, fighting over the sugar and the cake
19. Each says she is engaged to 诚; the politeness collapses
20. Both men appear; the women learn neither is named 诚, and unite against them
21. The women go inside; the men, alone and miserable, eat all the cake
22. The women forgive them on one condition: each must truly be named 诚
23. 高太太 arrives to fetch 高文, refuses 西西 as well — until she hears 西西 has money
24. 杰克 refuses to allow 西西's marriage unless 高太太 allows his own
25. 高太太 sees 白老师 and recognizes her from many years ago
26. 白老师 confesses: distracted, she put her long novel in the baby carriage and the baby in her bag, and left the bag at the station
27. 杰克 brings the very bag; it is his
28. 杰克 is the son of 高太太's late sister — so 阿龙's elder brother
29. An old book gives his father's name: 诚. 杰克 has been 诚 all along
30. All three couples are free; the story closes on being truly 诚实

outline.title: 城里的下午
outline.summary: In his city flat, 阿龙 waits for guests and eats nearly all the cake meant for them, teasing his servant about it. 杰克 arrives from the country and announces he means to ask 高文 to marry him. 阿龙 says he cannot until he explains something first — and goes to fetch a watch 杰克 left behind on an earlier visit. Play the eating comedy and the friendship: 阿龙 light and teasing, 杰克 serious. End on 阿龙 holding up the watch.
outline.recap: On a hot afternoon in his city flat, the rich and lazy Along eats every one of the cakes prepared for his aunt Mrs. Gao and cousin Gao Wen, joking that eating slowly would have got him only one. His friend Jack arrives from the countryside and announces he means to propose to Gao Wen that very afternoon. Along says that before he can marry his cousin he must first know who Jack really is — and fetches a watch Jack left behind on an earlier visit, refusing to hand it over because of the words engraved on it.

outline.title: 手表上的字
outline.summary: 阿龙 shows the words engraved on the back of the watch: 'to uncle 杰克, from 西西'. Cornered, 杰克 confesses everything: in the country he is 杰克, the serious guardian of a young girl called 西西, and to escape to the city he invented a bad younger brother named 诚 — in the city he simply becomes 诚. 阿龙 laughs and confesses his own trick: an invented sick friend, 班先生, whom he must 'go and visit' whenever a dinner is dull. The two agree everyone needs a way out.
outline.recap: Along reads the engraving — "to my dearest uncle Jack, from Xixi" — and forces the truth out. Jack confesses: in the country he is Jack, raised by a kind old man who left him a house and the duty of caring for his granddaughter Xixi, before whom he must always be earnest and careful. To escape, he invented a wicked younger brother named Cheng living in the city, so that "visiting my poor brother" lets him become Cheng himself. Along laughs and confesses the identical trick: an imaginary sick friend, Mr. Ban, who conveniently falls ill whenever a dull dinner threatens.

outline.title: 高文小姐
outline.summary: 高文 and her mother 高太太 arrive for tea. Alone with 高文 at last, 杰克 (whom she knows as 诚) tells her he loves her and asks her to marry him; she happily accepts. Then she explains why she could never have loved him otherwise: the name 诚 sounds so honest that her heart trusted him at once, and she has always known she would marry a man so named. 杰克 is overjoyed and quietly terrified.
outline.recap: Mrs. Gao and her daughter Gao Wen arrive; Along whisks his aunt into the next room, leaving Jack alone with Gao Wen at last. He confesses he loves her and she accepts at once, saying she already knew. But she adds that she has always known she would marry a man named Cheng: the name alone makes her trust him as honest, and she flatly rejects the name Jack as meaningless. Jack, terrified, quietly resolves to find a way to truly be called Cheng.

outline.title: 高太太的问题
outline.summary: 高太太 questions 杰克 closely — his money, his house, his parents. He admits the truth: he has no parents he knows of; as a baby he was found in a bag at the station and raised by a kind old man. 高太太 declares her daughter cannot marry a man found in a bag, and takes 高文 away. 高文 secretly promises to stay true and asks for his country address — and 阿龙, listening, quietly writes the address down for himself.
outline.recap: Mrs. Gao interrogates Jack from a notebook — his age, work, houses — approving of everything until she asks about his parents. He admits he never knew them: as a small child a kind old man found him at the railway station, inside a large black travelling bag. Appalled, she declares her daughter cannot marry a man found in a bag and refuses unless he can produce a parent within the week. Gao Wen secretly vows to marry no one else and asks for his country address; unseen at the door, Along listens and quietly copies the address into his own notebook.

outline.title: 乡下的西西
outline.summary: The country house. 西西 is meant to be studying with 白老师 but finds every excuse not to, and daydreams instead about 杰克's wicked younger brother 诚, whom she has never met. 白老师 lectures her about serious books. 陈先生 comes through the garden; he and 白老师 talk, both fond and both awkward, and go walking together, leaving 西西 alone and pleased.
outline.recap: In the quiet country garden, Cecily avoids her homework and argues cheerfully with her strict teacher Miss Bai about whether homework makes people good. What she really thinks about is Jack's wicked brother Cheng, whom she has never met but finds fascinating precisely because he is careless and troublesome. Miss Bai forbids the topic. Mr Chen arrives, and he and Miss Bai are so awkwardly fond of each other that Cecily gleefully sends them off for a walk — leaving her alone to daydream about Cheng.

outline.title: 诚来了
outline.summary: A guest arrives while 杰克 is away: 阿龙, introducing himself as 诚, the younger brother. 西西 can hardly believe the very person she has been dreaming about is standing in front of her, and he is nothing like the wicked man she was told of. They talk and laugh in the garden all afternoon; 阿龙 finds her clever and lovely. 白老师 watches uneasily.
outline.recap: While Jack is away, a well-dressed young man walks into the country garden and introduces himself as Cheng, Jack's brother — it is Along. Cecily drops her book: the man she has daydreamed about for months is standing in front of her, and he looks nothing like a villain. They take tea and cake in the garden and talk until sunset, she asking about the city, he charmed by her; she finds him effortless company. He hints he will stay whether or not Jack allows it, and she is delighted — while Miss Bai watches unsmiling from the window.

outline.title: 穿黑衣服的杰克
outline.summary: 杰克 comes home dressed all in black with sad news carefully prepared: his brother 诚 has died in the city, and so the lie can be buried forever. He is telling everyone this when 西西 runs in delighted to say his brother 诚 has arrived and is in the garden. 杰克 finds 阿龙 sitting there, alive and cheerful. He pulls him aside and orders him to leave at once; 阿龙 refuses — he likes 西西 and means to stay.
outline.recap: Jack returns dressed head to foot in black and gravely announces that his brother Cheng has died in the city — privately delighted, since burying the invented brother would let him finally be honest. Miss Bai and Mr Chen offer condolences. Then Cecily runs out with wonderful news: his brother arrived yesterday and is eating breakfast in the garden. Jack finds Along cheerfully eating cake, drags him aside and orders him to leave; Along, no longer joking, refuses — he loves Cecily and intends to stay.

outline.title: 西西的日记
outline.summary: Alone with 西西, 阿龙 (still 诚) asks her to marry him. She answers that they have been engaged for months, and fetches her diary to prove it: love letters she wrote to herself, the day they became engaged, even the day she broke it off and the day she forgave him — all before they had ever met. She adds that much of her love is the name itself: she could only marry a man named 诚. 阿龙 secretly resolves to become one.
outline.recap: Along proposes to Cecily, who calmly replies that they settled it long ago and fetches her diary as proof: dated entries recording their engagement, love letters, a quarrel, and a reconciliation — all invented before they ever met, the letters written by herself to herself. Along, charmed rather than alarmed, laughs. Then Cecily adds that half her love is for the name Cheng, and that a man called Along would have stirred nothing in her — leaving Along quietly determined to acquire the name for real, this very week.

outline.title: 两个人去改名字
outline.summary: Each man, without the other knowing, goes to 陈先生 to arrange to change his name to 诚 — and each asks for it to be done as soon as possible, this very week. 陈先生 is puzzled to be asked the same strange favour twice in one afternoon, and mentions it to 白老师. Comic near-misses as the two men just avoid meeting in the village.
outline.recap: In the village office Jack asks Mr Chen to change his name to Cheng, explaining away the oddity of taking his newly "dead" brother's name; Mr Chen books him for Saturday morning. An hour later Along arrives asking for exactly the same change to exactly the same name. Baffled but discreet, Mr Chen books him for Saturday too. That evening he mentions the strange coincidence to Miss Bai, who stops walking — and then quietly asks whether a wrong done many years ago can still be put right.

outline.title: 两位小姐喝茶
outline.summary: 高文 arrives at the country house looking for her 诚, and meets 西西. They are extremely polite to each other over tea — while quietly fighting: too much sugar, cake pressed on someone who asked for bread. Then each mentions she is engaged to a man named 诚, and the politeness freezes into open war, each producing her proof.
outline.recap: Gao Wen arrives at the country house while both men are out, and she and Cecily take tea with icy politeness — Cecily piling in sugar Gao Wen doesn't take and cake she didn't ask for, Gao Wen calling the eighteen-year-old a child. Each then announces she is engaged, and both name Cheng. The courtesy collapses: each insists he is hers, each offers her diary as proof, and they stand facing each other agreeing only that something here is very wrong.

outline.title: 没有一个叫诚
outline.summary: The two men walk in together and the truth comes out in front of both women: neither of them is named 诚. The women stop quarrelling at once, take each other's arm, and go into the house together, leaving the men outside. Miserable and alone, 杰克 and 阿龙 eat all the cake while blaming each other. Then the women call them in and forgive them on one condition: each must truly be named 诚. Both men happily report that this is already arranged.
outline.recap: The two men walk in and each woman greets "Cheng", forcing the truth out: one is Jack, the other Along, and neither is named Cheng. Gao Wen and Cecily take each other's hand and go inside, shutting the door. Left alone, the miserable men eat all the cake while blaming each other. Finally the women call them in and forgive them on one condition — each must truly be named Cheng — at which both men laugh, because they have already arranged exactly that for Saturday morning.

outline.title: 包里的孩子
outline.summary: 高太太 arrives to take 高文 home and refuses 西西 too — until she learns 西西 has money, at which she becomes charming. 杰克 refuses to allow 西西's marriage unless his own is allowed. Then 高太太 sees 白老师 and recognizes her from long ago. 白老师 confesses: distracted, she put her long novel in the baby carriage and the baby in her bag, and left the bag at the station. 杰克 fetches the bag — it is his. He is the son of 高太太's late sister, and so 阿龙's elder brother; an old book gives his father's name, 诚. He has been 诚 all along. All three couples come together, and the story closes on what matters: being truly 诚实.
outline.recap: Mrs. Gao arrives to fetch Gao Wen and refuses Cecily too — until she hears Cecily is wealthy, whereupon she approves; Jack counters that he will not consent to Cecily's marriage unless his own is allowed. Then Miss Bai appears and Mrs. Gao recognizes her: years ago she lost a baby, having absent-mindedly put her long novel in the child's carriage and the child in a large black bag left at the railway station. Jack fetches that very bag — he was the child. He is the son of Mrs. Gao's late sister and Along's elder brother, and an old book gives his father's name: Cheng. His lie was true all along. That autumn three couples marry, and the story closes on what matters: being truly honest.
